title: Locally dense subpresheaves preserve sheafified first cotangent homology
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $A\to B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $C\subseteq B$ be a subpresheaf of $A$-algebras (thus $C(U)$ is a subring of $B(U)$ containing the image of $A(U)$, and restrictions preserve it). Suppose that for every object $U$ and $b\in B(U)$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ with $b|_{U_i}\in C(U_i)$. For a commutative ring map $R\to S$, put $Q_{S/R}=R[x_s\mid s\in S]$, evaluated by $x_s\mapsto s$, and $I_{S/R}=\ker(Q_{S/R}\to S)$; polynomial rings and differentials mean [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Define
$$T_1(S/R)=\ker\bigl(I_{S/R}/I_{S/R}^2\longrightarrow S\otimes_{Q_{S/R}}\Omega_{Q_{S/R}/R}\bigr),\qquad\bar f\longmapsto1\otimes\mathrm df.$$
The restrictions on $A,C,B$ induce restrictions on these kernels, and the inclusions $C(U)\hookrightarrow B(U)$ induce a morphism of presheaves of abelian groups
$$\mathcal T_C\longrightarrow\mathcal T_B,\qquad\mathcal T_C(U)=T_1(C(U)/A(U)),\quad\mathcal T_B(U)=T_1(B(U)/A(U)),$$
using the presentation maps $x_c\mapsto x_c$ and the functorial kernel maps of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. The resulting map of abelian sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]
$$\mathcal T_C^\#\longrightarrow\mathcal T_B^\#$$
is an isomorphism. With the canonical $B=C^\#$ module structure on $\mathcal T_C^\#$ and the $B$-module structure on $\mathcal T_B^\#$ supplied by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], it is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Fix $U$ and put $R=A(U)$, $D=C(U)$, $S=B(U)$. For each finite subset $F\subseteq S$, let $D_F=D[F]\subseteq S$ be the subalgebra generated by $D$ and $F$, i.e. the values of polynomials in the elements of $F$ with coefficients in $D$. The polynomial universal property shows $D_F\subseteq D_{F\cup G}$ and $S=\bigcup_F D_F$, since $s\in D_{\{s\}}$. The family includes $D_\varnothing=D$ and is a nonempty directed family of $R$-subalgebras. The canonical presentations and their kernel maps exist and compose by the presentation-functoriality node; the same applies when $R$ changes under restriction.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), proof of the claim: directed system implicit in the use of Algebra Tag 07BQ

proof.text: For finite $F=\{b_1,\ldots,b_m\}\subseteq B(U)$, use the density hypothesis on each $b_j$. Repeatedly pull back the next covering to the preceding covering objects and compose the coverings. The site axioms give one covering $\{V_a\to U\}$ on which every $b_j$ belongs to $C(V_a)$; for $m=0$ use the identity covering. Each polynomial in these $b_j$ with coefficients in $C(U)$ restricts to an element of the subring $C(V_a)$. Consequently the actual ring map $D_F\to B(V_a)$ factors through $C(V_a)$: assign to an element its restriction, which lies in this subring; equalities and ring operations are inherited from $B(V_a)$. This factorization is compatible with $A(U)\to A(V_a)$.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), proof of the claim: finite generation and the covering on which the intermediate algebra factors through the image presheaf

proof.text: Prove local injectivity. If $s,t\in\mathcal T_C(U)$ have equal images in $\mathcal T_B(U)$, set $h=s-t\in T_1(D/R)$; it maps to zero in $T_1(S/R)$. Apply clause (ii) of the directed-union node to the family in step 1, starting at $D_\varnothing$, to obtain finite $F$ such that $h$ vanishes in $T_1(D_F/R)$. On the covering of step 2 the restriction square factors as $(R,D)\to(R,D_F)\to(A(V_a),C(V_a))$. Functoriality of the kernel maps says that the image of $h$ along this composite is precisely $h|_{V_a}$, hence is zero. Thus $s|_{V_a}=t|_{V_a}$.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), proof of the claim: Injectivity paragraph; work directly with a sectionwise kernel, as required for local injectivity

proof.text: Prove local surjectivity. Given $h\in\mathcal T_B(U)=T_1(S/R)$, clause (i) of the directed-union node gives finite $F$ and $h_F\in T_1(D_F/R)$ mapping to $h$. Choose the covering of step 2. Map $h_F$ along $(R,D_F)\to(A(V_a),C(V_a))$ to obtain $h_a\in\mathcal T_C(V_a)$. The composite to $\mathcal T_B(V_a)$ is induced by $(R,D_F)\to(R,S)\to(A(V_a),B(V_a))$, because both algebra maps are restriction of the inclusion $D_F\subseteq B(U)$. Composition of presentation kernel maps therefore gives $\varphi(h_a)=h|_{V_a}$. No choice of a lift along a surjection of section rings, and no flatness hypothesis, is used.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), proof of the claim: Surjectivity paragraph, with the omitted analogous argument written out

proof.text: Apply the local-bijection criterion to $\varphi:\mathcal T_C\to\mathcal T_B$. Steps 3 and 4 verify exactly its local injectivity and local surjectivity conditions, so $\varphi^\#:\mathcal T_C^\#\to\mathcal T_B^\#$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. The same criterion applied to the additive inclusion $C\to B$ (injective on each object; locally surjective by the hypothesis) shows that $C\to B$ is an abelian sheafification, $B$ being a sheaf. It is also a sheafification of presheaves of rings: if $g:C\to\mathcal G$ is a ring map to a sheaf of rings, its unique additive extension $\bar g:B\to\mathcal G$ is multiplicative and unital, since for $b,b'\in B(U)$ the covering of step 2 for $F=\{b,b'\}$ puts both restrictions in $C$, where $\bar g(bb')$ and $\bar g(b)\bar g(b')$ restrict to $g(b|b'|)=g(b|)g(b'|)$, and $\mathcal G$ is separated. Thus $C^\#=B$ as sheaves of rings, with unit the inclusion.

source.place: Tag 08TY (lemma-NL-up-to-qis), proof of the claim: conclusion that the locally bijective presheaf map induces an isomorphism of sheafifications

proof.text: The kernel-map node makes $\mathcal T_C(U)\to\mathcal T_B(U)$ $C(U)$-linear. Regard $\mathcal T_B$ as a presheaf of $C$-modules by $C\subseteq B$. The module-sheafification interface with $\mathcal O=C$ extends this map uniquely to a $C^\#=B$-linear map into the $B$-module sheaf $\mathcal T_B^\#$; on underlying abelian sheaves this is the map of step 5 by uniqueness of sheafification. Its inverse is $B$-linear: if $v=\varphi^\#(u)$ then $(\varphi^\#)^{-1}(bv)=(\varphi^\#)^{-1}(\varphi^\#(bu))=bu$. Hence the abelian isomorphism is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves with the stated canonical structures.
